name: Porphyry
biography: The Neoplatonist commentator on Aristotle's Categories, whose commentary had, per Russell, 'a very notable influence on medieval philosophy,' and who, Russell says, showed 'less caution' than Aristotle himself in treating a species as a kind of substance. Plotinus's friend, biographer, and editor, more Pythagorean and more inclined to the supernatural than Plotinus himself; his editorial arrangement of the Enneads pushed the Neoplatonist school in a more supernaturalist direction than Plotinus's own more restrained temperament, and his biography of Plotinus mixes credible material with miraculous legend (e.g. a story of a rival's magic spells recoiling on their caster).
